title: Evaluating an Offline Detector Against Adversarial Prompt Attacks
subtitle: A Reproducible Framework for Prompt-Attack Generation and Defensive Evaluation
contribution: A reproducible offline prompt-attack evaluation framework that reports both the stronger in-distribution result and the weaker novel-phrasing result, making the detector's generalization gap explicit instead of hiding it behind a random split.
methods: Generate adversarial and benign prompt corpora across defined attack categories.
Train/evaluate the offline TF-IDF + Logistic Regression detector.
Compare random, grouped-template, structural-fixture, and novel-phrasing OOD evaluations.
Keep live-model behavior claims out of scope unless separately measured.
evidence: Cited Python 3.12 CI: 175 passed, 1 skipped; 94.30% statement coverage, same test job.
Performance job 110120166630: OOD precision 0.5897, recall 0.92, F1 0.7188 on 25 adversarial and 25 benign hand-authored regression texts.
Grouped-template F1 0.9714 is an easier in-distribution reference. A prior random-split F1 of 1.00 is reported in source evidence, not independently confirmed by this audit.
Offline comparison of the same detector; these figures do not establish live LLM protection or population-level generalization.
limitations: Offline detector evaluation does not prove whether a live LLM would follow an injected instruction.
Structural fixtures are not equivalent to true OOD natural-language paraphrases.
No real-world jailbreak-defense rate is claimed.
reproduction: Install the documented development dependencies; run python -m pytest tests/ -q. Use the cited job configuration when reproducing coverage.
Benchmark data, adapters and environment requirements are separate; consult poster/13_reproducibility.md and the claim ledger.
